relevance_note: The paper reports an in-scope person with a germline TNFAIP3 variant, P10, for whom it prints "A variant in the tumor necrosis factor, alpha-induced protein (TNFAIP)3 gene (c.997dupG) resulting in a frameshift (p.A333fs^*2) was found in P10".
method_note: Read the full text, the schema and the rules; no script transcribed tables, all rows were written by hand from the Markdown. Scope: the paper is a 20-patient CVID WES cohort; only P10 carries a TNFAIP3 variant (Table 2; text: "A variant in the tumor necrosis factor, alpha-induced protein (TNFAIP)3 gene (c.997dupG) resulting in a frameshift (p.A333fs^*2) was found in P10"). Per the scope rule, patients with variants in other genes (P2 NFKB1, P3 STAT3, P11 IL17F, P12 IRAK4, P15 TTC37, P16 DDX41, P17 NLRC3, P18 TNFRSF1A/PLCG2) and patients with no candidate variant (P1, P4-P9, P13, P14, P19, P20) get no rows; they are counted in publications.cohort_size_as_stated = 20. P10 is labelled 'P10', the paper's own label (Table 1 header cell "| Patient ID |"). P10 is the single in-scope individual, so the checklist has 20 rows. Uncertainties and contradictions: (1) the paper never gives P10 an HA20 diagnosis - it says only "The clinical presentation of the patient shares many features with A20 haploinsufficiency", so disease_label_as_stated is the paper's own label 'CVID' and reports_individuals_with_tnfaip3_variant is true only because the TNFAIP3 variant is reported for an identifiable person. (2) Table 2 prints an ACMG classification as the bare number '4' for P10 (Table 3 lists TNFAIP3 under the citation '(23, 24)'), so acmg_criteria_as_stated is 'not reported'; the abstract's statement that three patients had variants "classified as likely pathogenic (NFKB1, TNFAIP3, and TTC37)" is a group statement and was used only for pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors. (3) The variant's origin is explicitly undetermined ("we have not been able to verify whether the variant is de novo or inherited"), so inheritance is 'not reported'. (4) No functional assay was performed by the authors ("we were not able to functionally validate identified variants in vitro or in vivo"); the truncation/degradation statement about the OUT domain refers to the cited p.A332X variant, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. (5) Table 3 gives inheritance 'Unknown' for P10, which agrees with (3). (6) The variant is frameshift, so the checklist items 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' and 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' were left 'not reported' even though the text reports nodular regenerative hyperplasia and pancytopenia, because a narrow finding does not exclude or match a broader/other checklist item and the paper does not name a gastrointestinal ulcer or an autoimmune cytopenia. (7) Supplementary Tables S3-S5 are converted with bare patient numbers, empty cells and stacked cell contents; per D-31 nothing there was assigned to P10 by position (its Table S3 prophylaxis cell is empty, and its 'After IVIG' pneumococcal-antibody value is ambiguous), so those fields are 'not reported'.

treatment_summary.value: immunoglobulin substitution therapy (IVIG); splenectomy; granulocyte colony-stimulatory factor (G-CSF)
span: All patients received immunoglobulin substitution therapy, except for one (due to anaphylaxis), and 13/20 received additional prophylactic antibiotics, mostly azithromycin (Table S3).
Splenectomy relieved some of the hypersplenism and improved thrombocytopenia, and the patient moreover received granulocyte colony-stimulatory factor (G-CSF) to avoid neutropenia.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: clinical diagnosis of CVID with whole exome sequencing of a TNFAIP3 variant
span: Patients with a diagnosis of CVID in the Department of Infectious Diseases, Aarhus University Hospital, were included under the following criteria:
Patient 10 was diagnosed with CVID 10 years ago and experienced severe disease with significant hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia with persistent CD4 lymphopenia, and pneumonias.
A variant in the tumor necrosis factor, alpha-induced protein (TNFAIP)3 gene (c.997dupG) resulting in a frameshift (p.A333fs^*2) was found in P10 (Tables 2, 3).

variant_type_as_stated.span: A variant in the tumor necrosis factor, alpha-induced protein (TNFAIP)3 gene (c.997dupG) resulting in a frameshift (p.A333fs^*2) was found in P10 (Tables 2, 3).

zygosity.span: A deleterious heterozygous 15 nucleotide (nt) deletion (p.P317_I322delinsL) and missense (p.N323Y) mutation in the nuclear factor-κB (NFKB)1 gene were identified (Tables 2, 3).

inheritance.span: The variant harbored by P10 has not been described previously, and we have not been able to verify whether the variant is de novo or inherited; however a p.A332X mutation has been reported in autosomal dominant familial Behçet disease and haploinsufficiency of A20 (35).

pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors.span: three patients had four variants in three different genes classified as likely pathogenic (NFKB1, TNFAIP3, and TTC37)
